errors.claim: MCP calls are logged to agent_calls (agent_surface.sql:39-50, agent-transport.ts:84)
errors.truth: Both REST and MCP calls are logged: restRequest and mcpRequest both run through logged(), which inserts into agent_calls after the reply (lines 53-64). Line 84 is only the method-name allowlist.

errors.claim: The write() scope check runs before any input parsing or database work
errors.truth: executeAgentTool parses the input with inputs[tool].parse(raw) at line 214 before calling write(); only the parse inside write() comes after the check. A read token sending malformed write arguments gets 400 invalid_arguments, not 403. The check does precede all database work and network tests.

errors.claim: A read token gets 403 insufficient_scope before any input is parsed
errors.truth: executeAgentTool parses the tool input at line 214 before write() runs its scope check, so malformed arguments yield 400 first. The check does precede all database work and network tests.

errors.claim: The most a write token can do is draft an incident update.
errors.truth: Read in context it is about incidents, but as written it understates write scope: a write token can also provision_app, create_monitor and pause.

errors.claim: I found no caller of its requireAgentPermission() helper, so the SQL check is what actually enforces it.
errors.truth: requireAgentPermission is called on every tool call (monitors:read) and again in write() (monitors:write or incidents:draft) before any DB read, ownership check or network test. A unit test asserts a read credential is refused with 403 for all four write tools before any DB or network call. The app-layer check is real; the SQL check is the second layer.

errors.truth: At this commit they are :94, :97, :98-101, :103, :104 and :107-126 (requireAgent starts at :86). Every cited line is off by about three.

errors.claim: A read-only token possibly causes activity and call logging (agent_activity and agent_calls tables set up for it in agent_surface.sql:58-59)
errors.truth: agent_calls is written for every REST/MCP call (best effort, after the reply), so that is definite. agent_activity is only inserted inside agent_write after a successful write, so a read token never writes it. Lines 58-59 are the revoke/grant statements, not the table definitions (30-50).

errors.claim: An OAuth connection can write if the member's role allows it
errors.truth: The OAuth path checks the member role only for monitors:read and then always assigns scope 'write'; no write permission is checked on the role. In V1 there is one admin role with every permission, so in practice every member's OAuth grant can write.
